reviews.title: Talabat lost a loyal customer who didn't
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Talabat for almost 3 years, spending so much money and always choosing them over other apps. But enough is enough!
This is the THIRD TIME IN A ROW I’ve faced the same nightmare! Today, my order was ready at 2:50 PM, and by 4:50 PM, NO RIDER had picked it up!
I contacted support SIX TIMES, and all I got were endless apologies and empty promises. They even called me, but NOTHING changed! The restaurant told me someone had already taken my order. So where is my food? DOES ANYONE EVEN KNOW?!
Hours of waiting, stress, hunger, endless calls, and absolutely no solution. Is this what customers are paying for?!

Today, I canceled my order and DELETED THE APP. You’ve lost a loyal customer of almost 3 years!

I was shocked to read the recent reviews and realize I’m not the only one experiencing this.

My advice? Order directly from restaurants or use another app. Save yourself the stress!
Talabat, loyalty means nothing when you don’t respect your customers. NEVER AGAIN!

reviews.title: Overpriced for Customers, Unfair to Businesses!
reviews.text: Honestly, Talabat has always been way too expensive. The prices of food, groceries, drinks, and even basic everyday items are ridiculously high. On top of those already expensive prices, customers have to pay delivery fees, service fees, and other extra charges. Sometimes, even ordering one or two simple items ends up costing way more than it should. What’s even more concerning is how much restaurants and stores might have to pay Talabat in commissions and fees. These businesses work hard to prepare and sell their products, yet a portion of their earnings goes to the delivery platform. I understand that Talabat needs to make money too, but the commission rates should be reasonable and fair for businesses. It’s frustrating to think that customers could be paying high prices while restaurants are also losing part of their earnings to platform fees. Talabat is supposed to make ordering easier and more convenient, not unnecessarily expensive for everyone involved. I really hope Talabat takes this feedback seriously, makes its prices more affordable, reduces unnecessary fees, and treats both customers and businesses fairly.

reviews.text:
Hello,

I have already contacted your customer support about this issue, but unfortunately, I still haven’t received any response.

I want to highlight once again how incredibly frustrating and inconvenient your app is when it comes to choosing a delivery address.

When I am not physically at home, there is no simple option to select my saved home address for delivery.

For example, when I’m on my way home and want to order food so that it arrives around the same time as I do, the app automatically uses my current location instead of allowing me to select my home address.

As a result, I have to manually enter the exact same home address every single time I place an order. This takes several minutes, and I have to repeat this ridiculous process almost every day!

Why can’t I simply select “Deliver to Home” regardless of my current GPS location?

This is such a basic feature that should exist in any food delivery app.

It’s extremely frustrating, unnecessarily complicated, and honestly makes me want to stop using your service altogether and switch to a competitor.

Please fix this issue and allow customers to select their saved home address regardless of their current location.

I would also appreciate an actual response to this feedback, since my previous message was ignored.

Thank you.

I contacted Talabat customer service, and after coordinating with them, I was informed that they could not take any action because the driver had taken a photo of the order along with my villa number and then left without actually delivering the food.

I have security cameras at my home, and they clearly show that the driver stopped in front of my villa number, took a photo of the order and the villa number, then took the order and left without delivering it to me.

Until now, the issue has not been resolved and I have not received a refund. I was told that because the driver documented the delivery by taking a photo of the order and the villa number, Talabat could not take any further action.

Honestly, this is completely unacceptable. Taking a photo of an order in front of a customer’s home does not prove that the order was actually delivered to the customer.

I have cancelled my Talabat Pro membership and I will never renew it again. Very disappointing experience, especially considering the size and reputation of Talabat.

reviews.title: Consistent pattern of pushing problems onto the customer - NOT USING TALABAT AGAIN
reviews.text:
I've ordered from Talabat multiple times, and the same issue keeps happening: when an item is missing from my order, the restaurant or shop calls me and says they can't cancel the order or refund the money. I just have to "choose something else" or take it up with customer service myself. This has happened repeatedly, and each time it's their error, yet I'm the one left chasing a resolution.

What makes it worse is the back and forth blame game. When I tell the restaurant it's their responsibility to resolve it with customer service, since they're the ones with the missing item, they turn it around and say "you're the one who wants to cancel, not us." I have to point out, again, "you're the one with the missing item, not me." It shouldn't take that much convincing to get a vendor to acknowledge their own mistake.

The most recent incident was the worst. A delivery driver arrived and told me he'd hand over the order, and I should contact customer service about the missing item. Then he called back and said he wouldn't give me the order at all, because if he did, he'd be blamed for the missing item, so I needed to call and cancel it myself.

This isn't a one-off glitch. It's a systemic issue where the burden of fixing Talabat's mistakes is repeatedly placed on the customer, with drivers and vendors pointing fingers instead of resolving things. Customer service shouldn't be something I have to escalate to every single time an item goes missing.

Talabat needs to start protecting its customers—not just the restaurant chains that generate business for the platform.
